name: Ulagalantha Perumal Temple (Thiruooragam), Kanchipuram
deity: Vishnu as Ulagalantha Perumal (Trivikrama), with the Goddess Amudhavalli Thayar — the Divya Desam of Thiruooragam, the main sanctum of a complex that holds four Divya Desams
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Pallava (with Chola, Vijayanagara and Nayak additions)
summary: In Kanchipuram, Vishnu rises as Ulagalantha Perumal, the Trivikrama who measured the worlds; his sanctum is the Divya Desam of Thiruooragam, and three more Divya Desams stand within the same complex.

sections.history: Thiruooragam is the Divya Desam of the main sanctum of the Ulagalantha Perumal Temple in Periya Kanchi, and one of the 108 Divya Desams of Thondai Nadu sung in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. The temple is believed to have been raised by the Pallavas, with later contributions from the Medieval Cholas, the Vijayanagara kings and the Madurai Nayaks, and inscriptions of the Pallava and Chola periods are recorded here. Three further Divya Desams — Thiruneeragam, Thirukkaragam and Thirukkarvanam — stand within the same precincts. They are believed to have once been independent shrines, and a single verse of Thirumangai Alvar names them together. The temple is administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu.
sections.architecture: The temple faces west, and its sanctum is crowned by the Srikara Vimanam. The presiding image is the towering Trivikrama, one foot raised as if to stride across the heavens, with Amudhavalli Thayar worshipped in her own shrine. The Naga Tirtham and the Shesha Tirtham are its sacred tanks. Within the walls, the three other Divya Desams have their own small sanctums in separate precincts, so that the visitor passes through four abodes of Vishnu in one complex.
sections.legends: The sthala purana recalls Vamana, the dwarf avatara of Vishnu, who came to the asura king Mahabali and asked for three paces of land. Granted the gift, he grew into Trivikrama, the Lord who measured the worlds, and when no place remained for the third step, Mahabali offered his own head. Tradition also holds that the Lord revealed himself here in a smaller form as Adisesha, the serpent — uragam in Tamil — which gives the shrine its name, Thiruooragam, and its deity the name Ooragathan.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava observances of Kanchipuram: Vaikunta Ekadashi, the annual Brahmotsavam with processions of the Lord through the streets, and the Margazhi recitations of the Divya Prabandham. As the four Divya Desams share one complex, their worship is woven into a single calendar. Confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: Come to Thiruooragam as to a pilgrimage in miniature. Having beheld the great Trivikrama, walk the precincts to find Thiruneeragam, Thirukkaragam and Thirukkarvanam, each a separate Divya Desam with its own Lord and Thayar, and the shrine of Adisesha. Allow time, ask the priests to point out each sanctum, and take the circuit slowly.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi and festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctums; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple stands in the old town of Kanchipuram (Periya Kanchi), reached by road from Chennai, about 70 km to the north-east, with Kanchipuram town the nearest railhead and Chennai the nearest major airport. Auto-rickshaws and local buses connect the Divya Desams of the town.
